persons.name: Tom
persons.harm: A friend of about four years (met through his disability advocacy group) obtained roughly $1,000 by Venmo, $2,500 by Zelle and further sums under false bail/bond and homelessness stories in May-July 2023, used his card details for many fraudulent charges, and (by her own admission on a jail call) opened a credit card in his name; he was left 'out like 15 grand' and in financial crisis.
persons.perpetrator_role: a friend he met through his disability advocacy group (the season's con artist)

quotes.quote: And again, by the way, this is just a bluff. I can't afford lawyers for crud and I'm not going to go to my parents for that because they've supported me through a lot.
And I tell her, you need to pay me. It's a civil matter, not a criminal matter anyway.

contacts.what_was_asked: Stop and reverse unexplained charges on his card
contacts.what_institution_did: Cancelled and reissued his card several times and reversed the fraudulent charges, refunding him.
contacts.quote: I would say there were between 10 or 20 charges that my bank reversed in that month alone, and I was able to get that money back.
contacts.what_happened_next: The bank's reversals covered the card charges, but the Venmo, Zelle and credit-card-in-his-name losses remained.
contacts.notes: Bank is a financial institution (no specific code). It also issued new cards repeatedly: 'the false charges kept pouring in and my bank kept forgiving them.'

contacts.institution: Indiana State Police (supervising sergeant on the case)
contacts.when: November 2024 (host presented the season's evidence; Tom's organized evidence supplied to host)
contacts.what_was_asked: Further charges for crimes not yet charged, including those against Tom
contacts.what_institution_did: Met with the host, received the evidence and testimony and were 'considering further charges'; no new charge is reported by the season's end.
contacts.quote: Throughout my week in Indiana, I had productive conversations with Indiana law enforcement who are still considering further charges.
contacts.what_happened_next: Season ends with the state investigation ongoing; host says other victims have connected with state police.
contacts.notes: No charge for Tom's losses is shown. Basis is the host's account. Alyssa: Tom was excited at the Sept 2023 arrest 'not even for crimes that she had committed against him.'

persons.outcome_quote: He's in some really financial crisis right now. I think that was the hardest one for all of us to swallow.
persons.decisive_work_quote: I would say there were between 10 or 20 charges that my bank reversed in that month alone, and I was able to get that money back.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: within June 2023, the same month the card charges began
persons.notes: Partial protection = bank reversals only. Tom threatened police/court and a demand letter but says it was a bluff; he never filed. He was contacted by the awareness group (an Indiana State Treasury official acting privately), not an institution. Texts were read on air in detail; Alyssa read his texts and bank statements ('he shared every text message. He shared the statements from his bank'); the perpetrator admitted the credit card on a recorded jail call (second witness). The anonymous Twitter Space victim with a disability who lost his job ('my job became collateral') is probably Tom but is not named; not coded separately. The host's closing mentions 'a victim who has told [perpetrator] repeatedly not to contact him since summer of 2023', possibly Tom: harassment continued after her Nov 2024 release.

persons.name: Kayla (rental scam, charged case)
persons.harm: Toured a Fishers home on Morgan Street, signed a DocuSign lease and paid between $600 and $1,700 to the perpetrator, who did not own it and kept moving the move-in date back; one of three charged victims.
persons.perpetrator_role: a woman leasing the home who sublet it to several people without the owner's permission (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Report fraud: paid a deposit/rent for a home the perpetrator did not own
contacts.what_institution_did: Took the reports, investigated, contacted the home's real owner and obtained the lease barring subletting; probable cause documents followed (charges filed about 16 months later).
contacts.quote: During the course of the investigation, police made contact with the actual owner of the home, who stated that [perpetrator] was leasing it from him.
contacts.what_happened_next: Charges filed April 2023.
contacts.notes: About 16 months passed between the reports (Dec 2021) and charges (Apr 2023); in that time the perpetrator kept defrauding others. Account comes from WRTV's reading of probable cause documents.

contacts.what_was_asked: Charges
contacts.what_institution_did: Charged nine felony counts (fraud, theft, corrupt business influence); arrest warrant issued; she turned herself in and bonded out.
contacts.quote: [perpetrator] has been charged with three separate felony counts of fraud and three separate felony counts of theft, as well as a felony count of corrupt business influence.
contacts.what_happened_next: Perpetrator released on bond April 28, 2023 and kept scamming while out on bond.

contacts.what_was_asked: Arrest of the perpetrator on her warrant (community sting)
contacts.what_institution_did: Officers stopped and detained her but released her because the active warrant was a non-extraditable bench warrant (the felony warrant had not yet issued).
contacts.quote: The charge was non-extraditable, so they basically just let her go.
contacts.what_happened_next: Community members kept hunting for her.
contacts.notes: Initiated by awareness-group volunteers acting on behalf of the victims generally, not by this victim. The warrant involved was from a different (misdemeanor) case.

contacts.what_was_asked: Appearance at pretrial hearing / bail revocation
contacts.what_institution_did: After she failed to appear, the judge issued an additional (extraditable) warrant.
contacts.quote: Because of this, the judge issued an additional warrant for [perpetrator]'s arrest.
contacts.what_happened_next: Perpetrator stayed in hiding in Airbnbs for weeks.

contacts.what_was_asked: Arrest on outstanding warrants at the Airbnb located through a community sting
contacts.what_institution_did: Deputies went to the address, were let in by the Airbnb owner, and arrested her.
contacts.quote: And he was like, well, I just wanted to let you know that we got her.
contacts.what_happened_next: Held in Hamilton County Jail from Sept 9, 2023; plea in November.
contacts.notes: Call made by a community volunteer after a fake-business sting run by community members.

contacts.what_was_asked: Conviction and restitution
contacts.what_institution_did: Accepted a plea to two counts (seven dismissed); 730 days with 365 suspended and jail credit, probation, and restitution of $1,300 to one victim and $600 to each of two others.
contacts.quote: For count 2, [perpetrator] was sentenced to 730 days in the Indiana Department of Corrections with 204 days of jail credit. Of the sentence, 365 days were suspended.
contacts.what_happened_next: Community corrections later revoked (April 2024) and she was ordered to serve 508 days; released Nov 15, 2024 owing restitution.
contacts.notes: Community members felt the sentence was light ('it just seems like the justice system kind of let us down here').

persons.outcome_quote: For count 5, [perpetrator] was again sentenced to 730 days in the Indiana Department of Corrections for the false leasing of the same property to at least three different individuals.
persons.decisive_work_quote: During the course of the investigation, police made contact with the actual owner of the home, who stated that [perpetrator] was leasing it from him.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about 16 months: reports in December 2021, charges April 2023 (conviction November/December 2023)
persons.notes: Named only by the perpetrator ('I believe that I've paid more to Kayla than what was stated on the court order'); which restitution amount is hers is not stated. The three charged victims never speak on the show; the perpetrator says only one wrote a victim impact statement. The 'protected' code reflects conviction and restitution order; whether restitution was fully paid is unverified (the perpetrator said in Sept 2024 she still had to pay 'roughly $3,000' on the Hamilton County case). Arrests that enabled the plea came from community stings; no code exists for community volunteers who are not victims or family.

persons.name: Victoria Hampton
persons.harm: In 2021, at age ~68-70, she paid the perpetrator $1,800 to sublet an apartment/home, never got keys or her money back, was left homeless and had to move to Arizona to live with a friend.
persons.perpetrator_role: a woman offering to sublet her apartment (the season's con artist)
persons.outcome_quote: But Hampton never got the keys or her money back.
persons.notes: Heard only through a WTHR news clip: 'For a year and a half, Victoria Hampton has been waiting for justice.' A community member says she is not on the charged case ('Victoria is not listed on the case that brought you in'), so whether she ever reported to police is not stated. The 'one of the victims was scammed out of $1,800 which led to her homelessness' and the woman left homeless at Christmas probably refer to her.

persons.name: [unnamed] woman who paid for a Saxony apartment sublease
persons.harm: In 2021 she paid the perpetrator $1,700 to sublease a unit in the District at Saxony apartment complex and never received a key.
persons.perpetrator_role: tenant illegally subleasing the unit (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Report: paid $1,700, never received a key
contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated the perpetrator for trying to sublease the unit; no charge is mentioned.
contacts.quote: September of 2021, the Fisher's police were investigating [perpetrator] for trying to sublease a unit in the district of Saxony
contacts.what_happened_next: She was paid back a month later.
contacts.notes: Whether the repayment resulted from the investigation is not stated.

persons.outcome_quote: The woman was paid back a month later.
persons.notes: One-sentence account from the host's review of Fishers police records. Coded protected because she got her money back after police became involved, but the story does not show that police caused the repayment; decisive work unclear.

persons.name: Edward Ma
persons.harm: A Canadian friend from the Twitter mental-health community; in 2022 the perpetrator, posing as Indiana's governor and other political figures and later as a lawyer threatening legal action, got about $5,000 from him for a promised place to live.
persons.perpetrator_role: an online friend who impersonated political figures (the season's con artist)

quotes.quote: I don't have money to pay for a lawyer. Even if I go for court, I'm not gonna get my money back.

It's important to note that part of the reason that Edward was more hesitant about going to police regarding the $5,000 that [perpetrator] had taken from him is because he was located in Canada at the time.

persons.outcome_quote: And the only thing I can do is talk about it. So I started talking on Twitter about it.
persons.notes: Other reason = cross-border jurisdiction ('this is going to be international'). A friend suggested local police. A community member: 'you will never serve a day in jail for what you did to Edward.' The perpetrator said in Sept 2024 she would pay him after the Hamilton County restitution. Possibly the second disabled victim referred to with Tom ('Did you specifically target Tom and **** because of their disabilities?'), but the redacted name is not confirmed.

persons.name: Linda (aunt)
persons.harm: In 2017 her niece took out credit cards in her name without consent and ran up over $20,000; she did not notice for close to a year.
persons.perpetrator_role: her niece (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Repayment of the stolen credit
contacts.what_institution_did: Entered judgment that the niece owed her $25,152.94.
contacts.quote: On October 26, 2018, there was a judgment in civil court.
contacts.what_happened_next: As of the season she was still owed $20,592.94; the perpetrator says the aunt is now considering dropping the suit.
contacts.notes: Who filed is not stated. A consultant reportedly 'learned that [perpetrator] was being investigated because of the financial theft against her aunt Linda', but no criminal investigation is otherwise described.

persons.outcome_quote: And as of today, she still owes $20,592.94.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: judgment in October 2018, about a year after the 2017 theft
persons.notes: Aunt never speaks. Only about $4,560 of the judgment appears to have been paid. The perpetrator's account (Sept 2024): 'My aunt is considering dropping a lawsuit... she regrets taking it out of the family.' Named by the show (first name used here).

persons.name: Seth (Bulldogs Moving Company)
persons.harm: His two-year-old moving company packed, moved and unpacked the perpetrator's home (about November 19, 2022) for about $5,000; she paid with a check from a closed account, then ghosted them.
persons.perpetrator_role: a moving customer (the season's con artist)

contacts.institution: Indiana civil court (collections case filed December 7, 2022)
contacts.what_was_asked: Payment of the ~$5,000 owed plus attorney fees
contacts.what_institution_did: Ruled for the company after she failed to appear; lawyers advised garnishment was pointless because she had nothing to garnish.
contacts.quote: I think she even missed actually going to court when she was supposed to, which I think is a reason why the judge ruled in our favor, because she just never even showed up.
contacts.what_happened_next: No money recovered beyond the $50 deposit.

persons.outcome_quote: Since then I don't think she's made any attempts to pay us.
persons.decisive_work_quote: So we ended up having to get our lawyers involved to be able to try to get the money and she wasn't cooperating with the lawyers as much.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: case filed within weeks; resolved May 23, 2023, about six months after the move
persons.notes: Partly protected: judgment obtained, but uncollectable. Seth also warned the second moving company she hired ('she used us a few months ago and she never paid us'), which then kept her goods in storage. A community member corroborates the bad-check/mover history.

persons.name: Stephen (Mason Motors)
persons.harm: His Utah company leased Teslas to the perpetrator: one in her own name, which she crashed without valid insurance, and a white Tesla leased under her former roommate's identity; she fell behind on payments, gave false insurance documents and told him a child of hers had died to delay paying.
persons.perpetrator_role: a lessee using her own and a stolen identity (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Insurance payout for the crashed Tesla
contacts.what_institution_did: Had not paid out.
contacts.quote: And he explained to me that he has not received the insurance payout for the Tesla of hers that she crashed.
contacts.notes: Reason not stated; documents she filed were later found false/uninsured.

contacts.what_was_asked: Damages (no less than $64,618) for breach, fraud, conversion, etc.
contacts.what_institution_did: Found for Mason Motors; judgment of $68,002.10 (host also says $68,210).
contacts.quote: And although Stephen and his company, Mason Motors, won the civil case, [perpetrator] has yet to pay the judgment of $68,210, and further criminal charges have not been pursued at this time.
contacts.what_happened_next: Judgment domesticated in Indiana.

contacts.what_was_asked: Make the Utah judgment enforceable in Indiana
contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered the judgment domesticated so wages/assets can be garnished in Indiana.
contacts.quote: The judgment in Indiana will be treated the same as any judgment issued by an Indiana court, meaning that the creditor, Mason Motors LLC and Stephen Mason, can take steps to enforce the judgment, such as garnishing wages or seizing assets in Indiana to collect the amount owed.
contacts.what_happened_next: Unpaid; the perpetrator says she has been advised to declare bankruptcy on the bigger debts.

contacts.what_was_asked: Criminal charges for the identity theft
contacts.what_institution_did: Consideration of charges said to be ongoing; none pursued by season's end.
contacts.quote: Today, consideration of criminal charges regarding the alleged identity theft related to the civil case regarding the Teslas is ongoing.
contacts.what_happened_next: No charges at season's end.
contacts.notes: Which agency is not named. A community member speculated they 'realized that they may not have the burden of proof for criminal charges'.

persons.outcome_quote: And although Stephen and his company, Mason Motors, won the civil case, [perpetrator] has yet to pay the judgment of $68,210, and further criminal charges have not been pursued at this time.
persons.decisive_work_quote: And he messaged back pretty soon after and said, yes, I've actually hired a lawyer to discuss this matter.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: lawsuit filed after October 2023; judgment domesticated July 2024
persons.notes: He did not give an interview; account via a community member (Alex) and the 128-page court filing the group obtained. He recovered the white Tesla himself (disabled it via the Tesla app and flew in) after Alex sent him proof she was driving it: self-help, not institutional. Community member Alex's information also contributed; no code for non-victim community volunteers.

persons.name: Abby Espy
persons.harm: Former roommate: allegedly bitten on the hand hard enough to bleed (Feb 2021), had her room rented out as an Airbnb/rental scam after moving out, and had her identity used to open a Lyft account and to lease a Tesla.
persons.perpetrator_role: her former roommate and friend (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Report of being bitten
contacts.what_institution_did: An incident report was made; no further step is described.
contacts.quote: February 15, 2021, [perpetrator]'s then roommate, Abby Espy, called Fisher's Police Department regarding [perpetrator] allegedly biting her on the hand, causing her to bleed.
contacts.what_happened_next: Conflict continued; more incident reports in August 2021.
contacts.notes: Coded per rule that a report with no further step shown is did_nothing_or_delayed; the story may simply not say.

contacts.what_was_asked: Mutual complaints about physical disturbances and taken property
contacts.what_institution_did: Several incident reports; no action described.
contacts.quote: During August of 2021, there were several Fisher's Police Department incident reports between [perpetrator]'s then roommate, Abby Espy, and [perpetrator] making different allegations about physical disturbances or leaving the property, taking things that belong to the other person.

contacts.what_was_asked: Not stated
contacts.what_institution_did: Not stated.
contacts.quote: I'm told that the last time Abby and [perpetrator] were in the same room and saw each other was during a civil court case between the two of them.

persons.outcome_quote: One agreement that [perpetrator] signed as herself and the other where [perpetrator] allegedly signed falsely using the alias of her former roommate and friend, Abby Espy.
persons.notes: Did not respond to the show. Identity theft (Lyft account May 2023, Tesla lease) is not shown reaching any institution on her behalf; criminal charges for the identity theft were 'under consideration' only. 'Somebody else probably has a really negative impact on their credit score' refers to her.

persons.name: Pastor Michael Anderson
persons.harm: When the perpetrator was 15-16, she texted a member of their congregation fabricated messages claiming the pastors had invited her to their home to watch them have sex, a false sexual-misconduct accusation.
persons.perpetrator_role: a teenage member of their church (the season's con artist)

contacts.what_was_asked: Address the false accusation
contacts.what_institution_did: Interviewed the girl, had the chief call her parents in, and confronted her with proof the messages were hers.
contacts.quote: The chief of police called her parents immediately and said, listen, you need to come down to the police station with [perpetrator] and we need to address an issue.
contacts.what_happened_next: The accusation was found to be fabricated; no charge for false reporting is mentioned.
contacts.notes: Account comes from the pastors' Facebook Live interview (Forensic Foreplay) excerpted on air.

persons.outcome_quote: They're claiming that it was found out that you had fabricated the text messages and therefore the allegations against them were false.
persons.notes: Named as the show names them (they are the harmed, falsely accused parties, not perpetrators). Co-victim: his wife, Pastor Stacey. The pastors said 'here's the proof that you said it'; whether their own evidence or the police's work was decisive is not clear.

coder_notes:
Season 22 centres on one perpetrator, a young Indiana woman who conned and defrauded many people (rental scams, fake bail requests, identity theft, impersonating politicians, false sexual-assault and murder-for-hire claims). Her name is replaced with [perpetrator] in all quotations. Most harmed people are fraud victims; the season is told largely by community members of a 'scam awareness' Facebook group, several of whom ran stings (posing as a journalist; inventing a fake massage business) that led to her arrest in September 2023. Those volunteers are not victims or family, so the decisive-work codes have no exact fit for them; this is noted in the relevant records.
Only the three Fishers rental-scam victims got a criminal conviction for their harm (plea to 2 of 9 felony counts, Nov/Dec 2023, restitution $1,300/$600/$600). Most other victims (Tom, Edward, the movers, the Tesla lessor, the aunt) got civil judgments or nothing; further state-police charges were 'under consideration' at season's end (Nov 2024).
Two stories with other perpetrators in the season folder were coded: E13 (Celisia Stanton, financial-advisor fraud) and the WCN Presents crossover with Madison McGhee (her father's unsolved 2002 murder).
Judgment calls: (1) Falsely accused people who are themselves the harmed parties (the pastor couple, Haribo, Elizabeth) are named as the show names them; politicians she falsely accused who are not heard (none tell their story) are not named or recorded. (2) Borderline emotional-deception records (Alex, Lainey, Alyssa) are included with low confidence; political acquaintances and community volunteers who were not themselves harmed are treated as witnesses/investigators, and one Facebook acquaintance who mentions being scammed is in others_mentioned. (3) A Facebook group's volunteer admins were not treated as an institution. (4) Where a police report is recorded with no further step shown, I followed the rule and coded did_nothing_or_delayed, although the show may simply not say more. (5) Banks are coded institution_type 'other'.
Process: reading was interrupted several times by usage limits. On the first resume notes.md was missing, so I re-read from s22_01 line 1 and rebuilt the notes. All 8 chunk files were read in full to their stated last lines, plus INDEX.txt and two unassigned data episodes. Quotes were checked by script against the transcripts, and sources were taken from the nearest preceding timestamp.
